info.title: Dameless
info.description: Play, review and analyze chess, with any UCI engine. Every command of the `dameless` CLI is one of these routes. Every request but `/api/health` carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

get.summary: Profiles side by side, with who leads each row.
Your Lichess connection as the app shows it.

post.summary:
Starts logging in to your Lichess account (OAuth with PKCE): open the link. Lichess sends the browser back to the
app's callback, which stores the token and sends the browser on to `return_to` with `?lichess=connected` (or
`?lichess=error&message=…`). The link works once, for ten minutes.
Opens a seek in the lobby for you (rapid or slower, the Board API's rule). The game starts when someone takes it.

delete.summary: Logs a connection out: forgets its token (revoking yours at Lichess). Games in progress go on at Lichess.

post.summary: Challenges from your account: a player (blitz or slower) or Lichess's AI (`ai_level`).

Accepts a challenge to you; the game starts on the event stream. 400 for one the Board API cannot play (bullet,
variants): accept that on lichess.org.
Declines a challenge to you.

put.summary: Stores a Lichess token after Lichess checks it: a person's account (not a BOT) allowed to play.

get.summary:
The machine's health for Settings: the analysis engine, the Maia engines, the disk and the database, each with
what to do about it.
Every drill, soonest due first.

post.summary: Makes drills from your profile's weak spots (new positions only); answers the drills made.

get.summary:
Today's drills: due ones first, then new ones up to the day's cap; or, with `theme` or `games`, a session on that
theme or opening line. They come as questions: the `fen`, `side` and `theme`, without the answer, which
`answer_drill` returns.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many in all (default 30; 10 for a theme or a line).

parameters.name: theme
parameters.description: Only this theme: a session on it, with the day's cap on new drills set aside.

parameters.name: games
parameters.description: Only drills from these games (comma-separated ids, at most 200): the games of an opening line.

parameters.name: max_ply
parameters.description: Only mistakes made by this ply (24 is the first twelve moves).

get.summary: Your drill hit rate over time, a point per day with a rolling mean (window 50 answers).

post.summary: Answers a drill (UCI or SAN): the outcome, the drill rescheduled, and the answer with its line.

The next hint at a drill, without the move: first what kind of move it is, then which piece moves. A hint is
remembered until the drill is answered, and a right answer after one counts half and comes back tomorrow.

get.summary: Every engine: the built-ins first (installed or not), then the engines you added; and the analysis engine.

post.summary:
Adds a UCI engine by path. It must answer UCI's handshake; what it calls itself (`id name`) is kept. 409 when the
id is taken (a built-in's or another engine's), 400 when the file is not a UCI engine.

put.summary:
Chooses the analysis engine: reviews, live evaluation, drills and the levels run on it. It must be installed and
play on the clock (Maia's fixed node cannot analyse: 400).

delete.summary:
Removes an engine from the list. A built-in's files stay (setup adds it again); when it was the analysis engine,
Stockfish analyses again.

get.summary: The evaluation sessions running now. A session that reached its budget is no longer listed.

post.summary:
Starts a live search. Its progress comes as `eval.info` events on topic `eval:<session>`; it ends at its budget,
when stopped, or when the policy turns analysis off.

delete.summary: Stops a session and waits until its engine has stopped.

get.summary: The live event stream.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Replay the kept events after this id. `Last-Event-ID` does the same for a reconnecting browser.

parameters.name: topics
parameters.description: Topics, comma-separated (`games,game:12,work`, `game:*`). None: every topic but `eval:*` and game detail.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The API token, for clients that cannot send headers (`EventSource`).

get.summary:
Lichess's opening explorer, as Lichess answers it. Needs your Lichess login (409 without it); refused while you
play on Lichess unless every game of yours is correspondence.

parameters.name: fen
parameters.description: The position as FEN; the start position when none.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: From this month (`2020-01`), or year for `masters`.

get.summary: Games, live ones first in the list's order of newest first.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Games started at or after this time (ISO-8601).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The page after this game (the last id of the previous page).

parameters.name: calibration
parameters.description: Calibration games between levels: left out unless `true` (only them) or `all`.

post.summary: Starts a local game: you against an engine, or two engines. Engines are started before the game is stored.

Stores pasted PGN as finished local games (one per game in the text). A player is you when `you` says so or the
tag names your Lichess account; anyone else is kept as a Lichess player of that name.

get.summary: A game as it is now: a live game's clocks, offers and your actions laid over the stored record.

post.summary:
Does an action as you in a game you play: 409 when the game is over or the action is not one of `Game.actions`
now, 400 for a move that is not legal. A move answers once it is on the board.

get.summary: A game as PGN, with a comment on every move (eval/depth, think time, nodes, clock).
A game's newest review (or the one by this engine and budget). 404 without one.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: The engine that reviewed it, by id; the newest review when none.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.description: The node budget per position; any when none.

post.summary:
Stops a live game: a game you sit in is resigned (aborted before each side has moved), an engine game aborted,
your Lichess game resigned there. Answers the game once it has ended, or as it stands after a few seconds.

get.summary: Whether the app is up. The one route that needs no token.
The ladder of levels with their calibrated ratings, your rating on it and the level suggested for you.

post.summary:
Queues calibration (background work at the lowest priority): levels play each other at fixed nodes, and the
ladder is refitted after each match.

get.summary: The calibration matches that would teach the most now: neighbouring levels, the widest and most even first.
Lichess's leaderboard at a speed.

Your opening lines with one colour: the named openings you play, your score in each, and how often you go wrong
in the first twelve moves, with the games to drill. Refused (409) while you play on Lichess, unless every game
of yours is correspondence.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Your newest finished games read, at most (500).

get.summary:
Your repertoire with one colour, from your games: the lines you play, where you leave theory, how you score.
Refused (409) while you play on Lichess, unless every game of yours is correspondence.

parameters.name: max_plies
parameters.description: How deep the tree goes, in plies (20).

parameters.name: min_games
parameters.description: A move shows once played in this many games (2).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Your newest finished games read, at most (500).

get.summary: What is known of a player.

post.summary:
Imports a player's finished games from Lichess (work, network only): `you` (your history, needs your login) or
`lichess:<name>` (theirs; refused while you play on Lichess).

get.summary:
A player's games added up: results over every finished game, engine figures over the reviewed ones, weak spots
for you.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only games from this time on (ISO-8601, or a date).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The newest games, at most (default 200); a number above how many there are means all of them.

get.summary: Your lines: your rating, accuracy and drill hit rate over time.

post.summary: Queues a review (work). Refused while you play on Lichess; a running review pauses while you do.

get.summary:
What setup would download (Stockfish 19, lc0 and Maia's nets) with the sizes GitHub gives, and what is installed
already. Downloads nothing.

post.summary:
Downloads the built-in engines into the data directory's `tools/` and adds them to the list, as work. Only on this
explicit request (the CLI shows the sizes and asks first).

get.summary: The status line's facts, and Settings › Machine.
The tablebase's answer for a position of seven pieces or fewer, as Lichess gives it. Refused while you play.

parameters.name: fen
parameters.description: A position with at most seven pieces.

get.summary: The API token, for pairing the hosted UI with this app (Settings shows it to copy).
Work running, queued and recently finished.
One work item.
A work item's log, as plain text. Lines also come live as `work.log` events.

post.summary: Pauses an item until it is resumed: a running one at its next safe point, a queued one is held.
Carries on paused work.
Stops an item: a queued one at once, a running one at its next safe point.

Account.description: A Lichess account as a connection knows it.

ActionBody.description: The body of an action; only `move` needs one.

Assist.description:
How much assistance is allowed now. Lichess forbids engines, books and tablebases during a game; its explorer is
allowed in correspondence only.

oneOf.description: Until stopped (the board's engine switch).

count.description: How many planned matches, when `matches` is not given. Default 3.

games_per_pair.description: Games per match, overriding each match's own (`core::levels::CALIBRATION_GAMES`, 20).

matches.description: These matches; else the plan's `count` most useful ones.

Challenge.description: A challenge to or from one of the connections.

color.description: The colour the connection would play.

id.description: Lichess's id, which becomes the game's id when accepted.

playable.description: Whether this app can play it (the Board API cannot play bullet or variants).

oneOf.description: None for unlimited games.

ChallengeEvent.description: The `challenge` event: what became of a challenge, with Lichess's decline key and a few words more.

id.description: The challenge id, which becomes the game's when accepted (an AI game's id at once).

ClassCounts.description: How many moves got each classification.

Classification.description: What a review calls a move.

Color.description: A colour chosen when starting a game or a challenge: a side, or let chance decide.

ConnectionKey.description:
A Lichess account linked to the app: yours, through the Board API. It is the only one, and stays an enum so games
and routes name it the same way everywhere.

playing.description: Games being played here through this connection.

Departure.description: Where a game first left theory, added up over the games that left at the same move.

by_you.description: You left theory, rather than your opponent.

example.description: The newest such game, to open on the board.

key.description: The last position in theory, and the move that left it.

score.description: Your points per game in those games, 0 to 1.

Drill.description: One drill and where its schedule stands.

oneOf.description: The last answer; `None` for a drill never tried (a new one).

best_moves.description: Every move that counts as correct (UCI), the engine's best first: all within [`CORRECT_WITHIN`] of it.

best_san.description: The same in SAN, for the answer.

due.description: When it is next due, and the interval that set it.

fen.description: The position to find a move in, and its key (the FEN without move counters), which drills are unique by.

game.description: The game and ply the mistake was made at.

line.description: The engine's line after its best move (UCI), shown with the answer.

played.description: What you played in the game, UCI and SAN.

reps.description: Passes in a row, and misses in all.

swing.description: Win percentage lost in the game.

DrillAnswerResult.description: What an answer came to: the outcome, the drill rescheduled, and the answer itself.

hinted.description: A hint was asked for first: a pass then counts half and the drill comes back tomorrow.

DrillAnswered.description: `drill.answered`: a drill was answered; the rescheduled drill follows as `drill.upserted`.

DrillHint.description: A hint at a drill: a nudge that names a property of the right move, never the move.

from.description: At level 2: the square the piece stands on, when all the right moves start there.

level.description: 1 says what kind of move it is, 2 which piece moves.

drills.description: In the order to play them: questions, without their answers.

due.description: How many of them are tried drills due again, and how many new.

started_today.description: New drills started today, counted against the day's cap.

total.description: Every drill there is, to tell "none yet" from "none today".

ElsewhereGame.description: A game of yours on Lichess that cannot be played here (bullet, a variant): it still turns analysis off.

Engine.description: An engine of the engines list.

analysis.description: Whether it is the analysis engine.

args.description: Arguments it is started with (lc0's `--weights=…` for Maia).

id.description: The slug seats and player keys name it by: `stockfish`, `maia-1500`.

id_name.description:
What it calls itself (its UCI `id name`), read when it was added or installed: `Stockfish 19`. Reviews and the
position cache are keyed by it, so a new release of an engine never reads an old one's results as its own.

installed.description: Whether it can be started: a binary is there.

levels.description: Whether the ladder of levels runs on it (the analysis engine, when it plays on the clock).

nodes.description: Nodes it searches a move whatever the clock: Maia's 1. None plays on the clock.

options.description: UCI options set after the handshake, before the app's own (`Threads`, `Hash`, `MultiPV`).

path.description: The binary; none for a built-in that is not installed yet.

rating.description: The rating it plays at, when it has one by design (Maia's nominal rating).

engines.description: Built-ins first (installed or not), then the engines you added, by name.

EntrantRating.description: An entrant's fitted rating: the estimate with its 95 % interval, and the games it rests on.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error answer: `{ "error": { "code": "conflict", "message": "…" } }`.

ErrorCode.description: The codes errors carry in the API's `{ error: { code, message } }`.

EvalBody.description: `POST /api/eval`: a live search of a position.

client.description: Who asks (a browser tab, a CLI run): one session per client, a new one replaces the old.

engine.description: The engine to search with, by id; the analysis engine when none.

fen.description: The start position as FEN; none for the standard start.

moves.description: Moves from it, UCI or SAN.

EvalLine.description: One line of a live evaluation. `score` is White's.

EvalSession.description: A started session: its events come on topic `eval:<session>`.

engine.description: The engine searching, by what it calls itself: `Stockfish 19`.

fen.description: The position searched, after the moves.

id.description: Monotonic; pass the last one seen as `since` (or `Last-Event-ID`) to resume. 0 on `reload`.

Event.description:
One event of the stream, as each `data:` line carries it: `{ id, topic, kind, data }`, where `kind` names the
payload's type. Every score in a payload is White's.

oneOf.description: At most five a second, never replayed.

data.description: At most five a second, never replayed.

oneOf.description: Never replayed.
Never replayed.
Not a domain event: the stream has a hole, so fetch what is shown again.

data.description: Not a domain event: the stream has a hole, so fetch what is shown again.

Game.description: The full record of a game.

actions.description: What You may do now; anything else is refused.

oneOf.description: While live: the clock each side holds now, in ms.

start_fen.description: The start position; none for the standard start.

GameChanged.description: `game.changed`: offers, what You may do, the clocks or the opponent's presence changed.

GameId.description: A game: played here, on Lichess, or imported.

GameSummary.description: What lists, events and the Games rail show of a game.

oneOf.description: Each side's accuracy from the newest review.
The side You played, if any.

GameThinking.description: `game.thinking`: the engine to move's progress. `score` is White's.

ply.description: The ply being chosen, so a late report for a move already played can be dropped.

GameUndone.description: `game.undone`: moves were taken back; `plies` is how many are left.

Health.description: `GET /api/diagnostics`: every item, and whether none fails.

HealthAction.description: What fixes an item: a label for the button, and the CLI command that does the same.

ok.description: Not failing (a warning or a note is still ok).

HitRatePoint.description: One day of the hit-rate trend.

hinted.description: Passes found with a hint, each worth half in the rates.

rate.description: Credit per answer that day, 0 to 1.

rolling.description: Credit per answer over the last `window` answers up to the end of that day: the line the UI draws.

max.description: At most this many games, newest first; all when none.

since.description:
Games started at or after this time (ms since 1970). Your history, when none (and no `max`, `speeds` or
`rated`): the games newer than the newest imported before and, until your whole history is here, every older
one.

oneOf.description: The side you played, when not found by your Lichess username in the tags.

JudgementCounts.description: Lichess's own counts: misses count as the mistake or blunder they are.

Leader.description: A row of the comparison and who leads it (indexes into the profiles; several on a tie, none without figures).

progress.description: Rating change over the last games.

LedgerSnapshot.description: The ledger as the status line shows it.

free.description: What work can still be granted.

oversubscribed.description: Live play holds more than the machine has, with work on top: games are played anyway, a little slower.

reserved.description: Held by live games and live evaluation.

Level.description: The ladder engine at one strength.

id.description: 1 is the weakest; the last level of the ladder is full strength.

multipv.description: Lines searched: the candidates [`choose_move`] picks among. 1 plays the engine's best move.

name.description: `Level 5`; the UI writes "Stockfish 1600" from the calibrated rating.

nodes.description:
Nodes per move. `None` is full strength: the engine plays on the clock, as in any other game (calibration
games give it [`FULL_CALIBRATION_NODES`]).

nominal.description: The rating the level was designed for, until calibration measures it.

temperature.description:
The softmax temperature, in win percentage points (0 to 100) of the side to move: a candidate that many points
worse than the best is chosen `e` times less often. 0 always plays the best move.

oneOf.description: The calibrated rating, once the level has games; else `null` (the UI says "about <nominal>").

suggested.description: The level nearest your rating (fitted, else Lichess's): the New game dialog's default.

oneOf.description: When the last fit was made.
Your fitted rating on the ladder's scale, once there is a fit with you in it.

return_to.description: The page to come back to: the app on a loopback address or the hosted UI (default the app's `/you`).

limit.description: At most this many new drills (20 when none).

Moment.description: A move worth linking to: the board opens the game at `ply`.

sacrifice.description: Pawns of material given up (brilliant moves).

url.description: The game on Lichess, at the move.

Moments.description: The best and worst of a player's reviewed games.

best.description: The brilliant moves with the most material given up (at most 3), else the great ones.

blunders.description: The worst blunders by win percentage lost (at most 3).

clock_ms.description: The mover's clock after the move (increment included).

oneOf.description: The mover's engine's own score, from White's point of view; engines only (and Lichess's analysis on imports).

NewEngineRequest.description: `POST /api/engines`: an engine you add by path.

id.description: Its id (a slug); made from the name when left out.

nodes.description: Nodes it searches a move whatever the clock (Maia-like engines); none plays on the clock.

options.description: UCI options set after the handshake.

rating.description: The rating it plays at by design, when it has one.

adjudicate.description: End decided games early (engines' scores only): resign at 3 moves of 300 cp, draw from move 30 at 6 quiet moves.

seed.description: Seeds the choices of seats at a level, so a game can be replayed; random when none.

Offers.description: Offers standing in a live game: who offered a draw, who asked to take back.

Opening.description: The opening as Lichess names it.

ply.description: How many plies the named opening covers: moves up to it are `book` in a review.

name.description: The opening family as Lichess names it, without the ECO code or the variation ("Sicilian Defense").

Opponent.description: Someone on the other side of a challenge.

OpponentGone.description: The opponent left a Lichess game.

claim_in_seconds.description: Seconds until a claim may be made.

average_rating.description: The opponents' average rating, over the decided games where it is known.

performance.description: A simple performance rating: the opponents' average plus 400 × (wins − losses) / games.

PhaseReview.description: One side's play in one phase.

accuracy.description: Lichess's game accuracy over this phase's moves, as lila's `phaseAccuracies`.

timed_moves.description: Moves with a known think time (games with a clock, after the first move of each side), and their total.

PhaseStats.description: Average game accuracy (each reviewed game counts once), overall, per phase and per speed.

PlannedMatch.description: A calibration match to play next.

a.description: The two levels, the weaker first.

priority.description:
How much the match is expected to narrow the ladder's intervals, relative to the others: the higher, the
sooner.

Player.description: Someone who sits at a board.

ratings.description: Lichess's ratings per speed, when known.

Policy.description: The fair-play policy, computed from the you connection.

reason.description: Why, while not `allowed`: "Analysis is off while you're playing on Lichess".

games.description: Finished standard games of yours with this colour that have a named opening.

lines.description: Most played first, then the flagged ones.

PrepLine.description: One opening line you play and how it goes.

drill_games.description: The newest games with an early mistake, to drill (`GET /api/drills/today?games=…&max_ply=24`).

early_mistakes.description: Your early mistakes and blunders in the line, and the win percentage they cost in all.

example.description: The newest game of the line.

goes_wrong_early.description: At least a third of at least three reviewed games had an early mistake.

moves.description: The line's moves (UCI) from the start, and as one PGN string (`1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6`); the position after it.

name.description: The opening's name: `Italian Game: Giuoco Piano`.

reviewed.description: Games of the line that are reviewed, and how many of them have a mistake of yours in the first twelve moves.

score.description: Your points per decided game, 0 to 1.

scores_badly.description: Your score is under 45 % over at least four decided games.

oneOf.description: The costliest early mistake, to open on the board.

Priority.description:
Which work runs first when cores are short: the lower, the sooner. Live games and live evaluation reserve their
cores outside the queue; these order the work items. The numbers are what the store keeps.

counts.description: Classifications in all reviewed games, and per game.

games.description: Games considered, of them reviewed, and the rest.

history_complete.description:
Whether your whole Lichess history has been imported, so later imports only look for new games. Only your own
profile fills it.

judgements.description: Lichess's own counts (a miss counts as its mistake or blunder).

openings.description: The most played opening families, at most 8.

rating.description: The rating in the newest game considered.

themes.description:
The same mistakes grouped by theme, the costliest first (every one, not just the listed weak spots); filled
for You only.

unreviewed_total.description:
All the player's games not reviewed by any engine yet, whatever the filter: what "Review all" does. Only a
single profile fills it; `None` when unknown.

weak_spots.description: Positions from the player's mistakes, recurring themes first; filled for You only.

ProfileFilter.description: Which games a profile adds up.

oneOf.description: Only games from this moment on.

speeds.description: Only these speeds; empty for all.

Progress.description: How far along a piece of work is.

text.description: One sentence for people: "12 of 40 games".

oneOf.description: The game the point comes from, to open it.

provisional.description: Lichess calls a rating provisional until it has settled (`prov`).

Ratings.description: Lichess's ratings per speed, when known.

departures.description: Where games left theory, the most common first (empty without a theory predicate).

nodes.description: The start position first, then by ply and by games.

RepertoireMove.description: A move from a position, with the games that played it and how you scored after it.

leaves_theory.description: The position it leads to is out of theory while this one was in (`None` without a theory predicate).

next.description: The key of the position it leads to.

score.description: Your points per game after it, 0 to 1.

ply.description: The fewest plies it was reached in.

theory.description: Whether it is theory (`None` without a theory predicate).

your_turn.description: Whether you are to move here: then `moves` are your choices, else what you met.

RepertoireOptions.description: How deep and how wide the tree is.

max_plies.description: Plies from the start read into the tree.

min_games.description: Moves (and positions) seen in fewer games are left out, the start position aside.

Review.description: A stored review: the summary and every move.

engine.description: The engine that reviewed it, by the name it reports (its UCI `id name`): `Stockfish 19`.

ReviewBody.description: `POST /api/reviews`: some games, or a player's newest games no engine has reviewed yet.

background.description:
Review in the background: at the lowest priority (`background`, beside calibration), and in a lane of its own, so a review asked for meanwhile runs at once. With `player` and no `limit`: every game of
theirs not reviewed yet, newest first.

concurrency.description:
Engines at once. When none: half the machine's cores; in the background, all of them (it gives them back
within one search when live play or other work needs them).

engine.description: The engine to review with, by id; the analysis engine when none.

limit.description: How many of the player's games; 20 when none, at most 1000. In the background: every one when none.

oneOf.description: This player's newest finished games no engine has reviewed: `you`, `engine:<id>`, `lichess:<name>`.

engine.description: The engine that reviewed it, by the name it reports (its UCI `id name`): `Stockfish 19`.

middlegame_ply.description: The ply whose move starts the middlegame and the endgame (1 = the first move), when the game got there.

ReviewUpserted.description: `review.upserted`: a game was reviewed; fetch the review for detail.

ReviewedMove.description:
One move as the review judged it. Scores are White's (`{cp}` or `{mate}`; `mate: 0` is the side to move
checkmated, after the game's last move); win percentages and accuracy are the mover's.

accuracy.description: Lichess's accuracy of this move, 0 to 100.

best_uci.description: The engine's best move here, and its line (at most 8 moves, UCI).

clock_before_ms.description: The mover's clock before the move, in a game with a clock.

cp_loss.description: Centipawns lost, each score capped at ±1000.

depth.description: The depth of the search of the position before the move.

eval_after.description: The engine's best score after it.

eval_before.description: The engine's best score before the move.

oneOf.description: Lichess's judgement, which a `miss` also carries.

phase.description: The phase of the position the move was played from.

sacrifice.description: Pawns of material given up along the engine's best reply (a brilliant move gives up 2 or more).

second_uci.description: The second-best move and its score, when there was a second legal move.

Score.description:
A score: centipawns, or a forced mate in so many moves. `{"cp": 31}` or `{"mate": -3}`. From White's point of view
unless a function says otherwise; `mate: 0` means the side to move is checkmated, from either point of view.

Seat.description: Someone at a board, as this game knew them.

engine.description: What an engine seat's engine called itself (its UCI `id name`): `Stockfish 19`, `Lc0 v0.32.1`.

level.description: The level of the ladder an engine seat played at (or Lichess's AI level); none at full strength.

name.description:
What to show: "You" is shown as the Lichess username when linked; an engine seat by the engine's name, or at a
level of the ladder by its rating ("Stockfish 1650").

SeatAction.description:
What a seat can do in a game. One set for every game, local or on Lichess; `Game.actions` lists those You may do
now. A move carries its UCI in the request, not here.

SeatRequest.description: `you`, an engine's id (`stockfish`, `maia-1500`), or `<engine id>@<level>` for a level of the analysis engine's ladder (`stockfish@5`). The object `{ player, level? }` reads too.

SetupPlan.description: `GET /api/setup`: what `POST /api/setup` would download, and what is installed already.

bytes.description: Everything together, of the sizes known.

installed.description: The packages installed already (they are skipped).

notes.description: What cannot be installed here, for people: "lc0 publishes no build for this platform: put lc0 on the PATH".

SetupRequest.description: `POST /api/setup`: which packages to install; all when empty.

SidePair_Option_f32.description: One value per side, such as both clocks or both accuracies.

SidePair_f32.description: One value per side, such as both clocks or both accuracies.

SidePair_u64.description: One value per side, such as both clocks or both accuracies.

acpl.description: Average centipawn loss, as Lichess computes it.

time_trouble_blunders.description: Blunders (Lichess's judgement) played with less than a tenth of the starting clock left.

oneOf.description: Played here, or pasted in as PGN.
Played through your Lichess connection.
History read from Lichess: `owner` is whose history it is (you, or another player).

Speed.description: Lichess's speeds, from its estimate of a game's length (initial + 40 × increment).

oneOf.description: None for games without a speed (movetime or node limits).
A FEN (or `startpos`) and moves played from it (UCI or SAN).

StartFrom.description: Where a game starts, when not from the standard position.

Status.description: The app and the machine it runs on.

lichess_url.description: The Lichess the connections talk to.

next_event.description: The id the next event will get.

policy.description: Fair play: whether analysis is allowed now.

stopped.description: False when it had already ended.

oneOf.description: The engines list: installing the built-in engines.

Subject.description: What a piece of work is about, so the UI can link to it.

Theme.description:
What a drill is about: the opening family of its game, the phase it came from, and what the mistake was about
(`core::themes`; `other` until a drill from before themes is classified).

detail.description: The cause the evidence names (`a knight`, `fork`), when it does.

ThemeCount.description: A name counted: a cause of a theme's mistakes, or an opening they came in.

ThemeStat.description:
Your mistakes of one theme (`core::themes`) added up: how often, how much they cost, and the costliest examples.
Every mistake and blunder in the games considered has exactly one theme, so the themes add up to all of them.

causes.description: The causes named most often (`a knight`, `fork`), at most 3; empty when the theme names none.

count.description: Mistakes and blunders of this theme, and the games they were in.

examples.description: The costliest, at most 3, to open on the board.

openings.description: The opening families they came in most often, at most 3.

share.description: Their share of everything lost to mistakes, 0 to 1.

swing.description: Win percentage lost to them in all, and per reviewed game.

oneOf.description: A clock per side and an increment per move.
Lichess's correspondence: days per move.
A fixed time per move, no clock.
A fixed number of nodes per move: no clock, so speed does not count, only search and evaluation.

TimeControl.description: How long each move may take.

TimeStats.description: Think time per move, from reviewed games with a clock (Lichess records no time for each side's first move).

time_trouble_blunders.description: Blunders played with less than a tenth of the starting clock left, in all and per game.

Timestamp.description:
A moment as an ISO-8601 UTC string, always written `2026-10-25T14:32:07.123Z` so they sort as text. `core` never
reads a clock: whoever makes one passes the time in (milliseconds since the epoch, or a string from Lichess or the
database).

TrendPoint.description: One game on the trend line, oldest first.

accuracy.description: The player's accuracy in it, when reviewed.

points.description: 1, ½ or 0; none for an unfinished game.

rating.description: The player's rating in it, when known.

score.description: Points scored, as a percentage of the decided games.

WeakSpot.description: A position before one of the player's mistakes or blunders in a reviewed game, to play out again.

kind.description: What the mistake was about (`core::themes`), and the cause when the evidence names one.

played.description: What was played, and what was better, in SAN.

recurring.description: How many weak spots share this one's opening family and phase: recurring themes come first.

paused_for.description: Why it is paused, for people: "Your Lichess game", "Live analysis".

WorkLists.description: The queue as people see it.

queued.description: In the order it will run.

WorkLog.description: `work.log`: one line of a work item's log.

YouSeek.description: Your seek in the lobby, open until someone takes it.

elsewhere.description: Your games on Lichess that cannot be played here.

seek_note.description: How the last seek went, for people.
